title: flashes
blurb: pictures, on top of whatever you were doing.

margin.t: everyone turns this one on first.

blocks.text: You put pictures in a folder. Every so often the app throws a handful of them onto the screen, at random spots, over whatever window you had open. They fade out on a timer, or you click them away. That is the whole feature, and it is the one most people turn on first.

blocks.caption: images land on top of the work, not beside it

blocks.text: Nothing is bundled and nothing is fetched. It only ever shows files you put there yourself, or images from a content pack you chose to install. If the folder is empty, nothing appears and no error is raised.

Two sliders decide how much arrives. Per Hour is how many times an hour a flash event fires. Images is how many pictures come with each one. Turned all the way up, that is an event every twenty seconds carrying twenty pictures, on every monitor you have connected.

blocks.caption: per hour is the spacing. images is what each one carries.

items: Point Flash Images at a folder that has pictures in it.
Leave Per Hour and Images near their defaults for the first session.
Set Fade above zero so images ease in rather than cut.
Turn the feature on, and watch one full cycle before you change anything.

blocks.text: Turned up, this puts high contrast imagery on screen up to 180 times an hour at full opacity with an instant cut. Flashing imagery can trigger symptoms in people with photosensitive epilepsy. Fade, Opacity and Per Hour are the three controls that bring it down; Enable switches it off outright.

Animated GIF and animated WebP both play, and they play their own animation on top of the flash rate rather than instead of it. Hydra mode changes what a click does: instead of dismissing an image, clicking it spawns two more. It is off by default and it is not subtle when it is on.

A flash is a window, and a window is not a screenshot. Flashes are marked as excluded from capture, so a recording or a screen share of your desktop will not contain them. That is deliberate, and it means you cannot record what a session actually looked like from inside the app.
